summary:
SP rating is the story of the last two weeks: R1 and R2 both sit at 59-60% over the last 14 days (60-42, 59-42, n=102 each) against season marks in the 53% range — a genuine +5.9pt spike flagged HOT on both models. That matters today because three of four games on the board are legitimate SP-driven spots. CHC @ SDP pulls full consensus across all four ratings on SDP, with R1 leading at +1.03 — and with SP humming hot for R1/R2, King-over-Boyd is the shape of play the model is currently cashing. BOS @ NYY is the inverse signal: all four ratings back NYY, topped by R4 at +1.12, but NYY the team has been brutal when picked this year (21-22, 49%, and strong plays -5.0u) — a spot where the rating consensus may be running into a team-specific bias worth shading down. PHI @ ATL is clean full-consensus ATL, R4 again strongest at +0.88, and with runs now hot for R3 (60%, +5.9pts) and R4 (60%, +5.5pts) this game lines up nicely if ATL's run-differential edge is driving the number.

The other three ratings aren't sleeping either — R3 has both runs and hitting flagged hot (60% and 55% respectively, both +5.9pts over baseline), giving it the widest hot footprint of the group, while R4's runs are hot at 60% too. Bullpen and bullpen_fatigue remain dead weight across every rating (46% each, no hot flags) — don't lean on either category today even where it lines up with a pick. Strong-play units confirm the hot streak is real money: R1 30-13 (+20.0u) and R3 30-13 (+19.0u) over the last 14 days, both around 70%, though all four ratings went cold on strong plays in the last 7 days (2-4 or worse, negative units) — a short-term dip that shouldn't override the 14-day trend given the small n=4-6 samples. CHW @ HOU is the one game where the board is soft — CHW consensus but deltas are thin (-0.01 to -0.40), the weakest-conviction game of the slate and one to treat as a pass or minimum stake regardless of category overlap.
